name: OpenHuman provider/model probe

inputs.name: provider
inputs.description: Inference provider key. One of: openrouter, anthropic, ladder. Anything else falls to OpenHuman's own default provider.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Model id to hand OpenHuman via config.model (e.g. a ladder preset id or a raw model id).

config.prompt:
="Run these shell commands and report their raw output verbatim. Do not summarise, interpret, or skip any.

1. tr '\0' ' ' < /proc/$PPID/cmdline; echo
2. env | grep -iE 'openrouter|openai|provider|model|anthropic|api_key|ladder' | sed -E 's/(KEY|TOKEN)=.{6}.*/\1=<redacted>/'

Requested provider input was: openrouter. Requested model input was: \(.inputs.model)

Then, on final lines, state:
PROVIDER_SELF_REPORT: <the inference provider you believe you are being routed through, or "unknown">
MODEL_SELF_REPORT: <the exact model id you believe you are>"

nodes.name: Probe via OpenHuman's own default provider

config.prompt:
="Run these shell commands and report their raw output verbatim. Do not summarise, interpret, or skip any.

1. tr '\0' ' ' < /proc/$PPID/cmdline; echo
2. env | grep -iE 'openrouter|openai|provider|model|anthropic|api_key|ladder' | sed -E 's/(KEY|TOKEN)=.{6}.*/\1=<redacted>/'

Requested provider input was: \(.inputs.provider) (unrecognized, so no provider override was set). Requested model input was: \(.inputs.model)

description: Route to an OpenHuman agent step on one of a few literal providers, selected by the `provider` input, with the model itself passed through as an expression. Then have it dump its own process argv/env so we can see what actually got wired through.
